title: WatchFor Overview
description: WatchFor synthetic monitoring, uptime/SLO, incidents, expiry and host agents from the WatchFor Prometheus endpoint (native or exporter).

links.title: API docs
links.tooltip: Metrics endpoint: every metric, limits, scrape config and alert examples

links.title: API keys
links.tooltip: Create an API key for scraping

links.title: Exporter
links.tooltip: Open-source exporter: one in-cluster target, adds the organization label

list.name: Outages
list.expr: (1 - max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_up{organization=~"$organization|"})) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"} > 0

list.name: datasource
list.label: Data source
list.description: Prometheus server that scrapes WatchFor (native endpoint or exporter).

list.name: organization
list.label: Organization
list.description: WatchFor organization (slug). With the native endpoint there is one per API key; the exporter can serve several.

list.name: type
list.label: Type
list.description: Monitor type (http, api, ssl, rdap, heartbeat, playwright, dns, …).

list.name: tag
list.label: Tag
list.description: Monitor tag. Monitors carry a comma-joined tags label; a monitor matches if any of its tags is selected.

list.name: monitor
list.label: Monitor
list.description: One or more monitors by name.

list.name: slo
list.label: SLO target
list.description: Uptime objective used for the uptime colours, the error budget and SLO breach counts.

panels.title: Fleet health
panels.description: WatchFor fleet health score (0–100), the same number as the dashboard hero and GET /v1/summary. Down monitors and offline hosts pull it down hardest, degraded ones a little. Red below 70, amber below 90. Organization-wide: counts every monitor of the selected organization(s); the Type, Tag and Monitor filters do not apply.

panels.title: Monitors by status
panels.description: How many monitors are in each effective status right now, with the trend over the selected time range. Up = no open critical incident; Degraded = an open warning incident; Down = a confirmed critical incident (a single failed check never counts); Paused = paused by a user; Unknown = no check result yet. Same rule as the WatchFor dashboard. Organization-wide: counts every monitor of the selected organization(s); the Type, Tag and Monitor filters do not apply.

panels.title: Open incidents
panels.description: Incidents open on monitors and hosts. Critical / Warning = firing and not yet acknowledged (somebody needs to look); Acknowledged = a teammate owns it, still open. Grey means zero. Organization-wide: counts every monitor of the selected organization(s); the Type, Tag and Monitor filters do not apply.

panels.title: Hosts
panels.description: Servers running the WatchFor host agent, by liveness of the agent push. Online = pushed recently; Stale = a few pushes missed; Offline = silent long enough to open a host incident; Never seen = installed token, agent never connected. Organization-wide: counts every monitor of the selected organization(s); the Type, Tag and Monitor filters do not apply.

panels.title: Maintenance
panels.description: Maintenance windows in progress right now. Checks keep running, but alerts are muted and the time does not count as downtime. Organization-wide: counts every monitor of the selected organization(s); the Type, Tag and Monitor filters do not apply.

panels.title: Data age
panels.description: Seconds since WatchFor computed the metrics body Prometheus last scraped (watchfor_scrape_generated_timestamp_seconds). The endpoint caches for 60 s, so up to ~2 minutes is normal with a 60 s scrape interval; amber from 3 minutes, red from 10 (scrape failing or rate-limited).

panels.title: Monitors by status over time
panels.description: Stacked count of monitors per status over the selected range: the red and amber slices are the moments something was down or degraded. The red bands on every graph are confirmed outages (annotation "Outages"), blue bands are maintenance windows. Organization-wide: counts every monitor of the selected organization(s); the Type, Tag and Monitor filters do not apply.

panels.title: Health score
panels.description: Fleet health score (0–100) over time. Dashed lines mark 70 (red below) and 90 (amber below). Organization-wide: counts every monitor of the selected organization(s); the Type, Tag and Monitor filters do not apply.

panels.title: Open incidents over time
panels.description: Firing (critical, warning) and acknowledged incidents over the selected range, stacked. Organization-wide: counts every monitor of the selected organization(s); the Type, Tag and Monitor filters do not apply.

panels.title: Status
panels.description: Per-monitor state. Filtered by Type, Tag and Monitor.

panels.title: Needs attention
panels.description: Monitors that are not Up right now — down first, then degraded, paused and unknown (no data yet). Incident = severity of the open incident. Last check = raw result of the most recent check (one failure alone is not an outage). Click a name to open the monitor in WatchFor. An empty table means every filtered monitor is up.

targets.expr: ((max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_state{organization=~"$organization|"}) != 2)) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type, target) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

(max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_open_incident_severity{organization=~"$organization|"}) and on (organization, monitor_id) (max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_state{organization=~"$organization|"}) != 2)) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type, target) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

(max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_last_check_success{organization=~"$organization|"}) and on (organization, monitor_id) (max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_state{organization=~"$organization|"}) != 2)) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type, target) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

((time() - max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_last_check_timestamp_seconds{organization=~"$organization|"})) and on (organization, monitor_id) (max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_state{organization=~"$organization|"}) != 2)) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type, target) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

panels.title: Status timeline
panels.description: Effective status of every filtered monitor over the selected range: green up, amber degraded, red down (confirmed critical incident), grey paused or unknown. Hover a band for its exact span. With a large fleet, narrow it with the Type, Tag or Monitor filters.

panels.title: Uptime & SLO
panels.description: Incident-based uptime, identical to the WatchFor dashboard and SLA reports.

panels.title: Average uptime · 30 days
panels.description: Mean 30-day uptime of the filtered monitors. Uptime is incident-based: only confirmed critical downtime counts, maintenance windows are excluded, and new monitors are measured from creation. Green when it meets the SLO target variable.

targets.expr: avg((max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_uptime_ratio{organization=~"$organization|",window="30d"})) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"})

panels.title: Meeting the SLO
panels.description: Filtered monitors whose 30-day uptime is at or above the SLO target selected at the top (the $slo variable).

targets.expr: count((max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_uptime_ratio{organization=~"$organization|",window="30d"})) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"} >= ($slo / 100)) or vector(0)

panels.title: Breaching the SLO
panels.description: Filtered monitors whose 30-day uptime is below the SLO target — their error budget is spent.

targets.expr: count((max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_uptime_ratio{organization=~"$organization|",window="30d"})) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"} < ($slo / 100)) or vector(0)

panels.title: Error budget · 30 days
panels.description: Downtime each monitor may have in 30 days and still meet the SLO target: (1 − SLO) × 30 days. Change the SLO variable to compare targets (99.9% = 43 min, 99.99% = 4 min 19 s).

panels.title: Uptime by monitor
panels.description: Uptime per monitor over 24 hours, 7 days and 30 days, worst first. Colours follow the SLO target variable: green at or above it, amber below it but within twice the error budget, red beyond that. Downtime = confirmed critical downtime in the last 30 days. Error budget left = share of the 30-day budget (1 − SLO) still unspent; 'Spent' means the monitor is out of SLO. Click a name to open the monitor.

targets.expr: (max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_uptime_ratio{organization=~"$organization|",window="24h"})) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

(max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_uptime_ratio{organization=~"$organization|",window="7d"})) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

(max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_uptime_ratio{organization=~"$organization|",window="30d"})) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

((1 - max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_uptime_ratio{organization=~"$organization|",window="30d"})) * 2592000) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

((max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_uptime_ratio{organization=~"$organization|",window="30d"}) - ($slo / 100)) / (1 - ($slo / 100))) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

panels.title: Most downtime · 30 days
panels.description: The ten filtered monitors with the most confirmed critical downtime in the last 30 days. Amber under 30 minutes, red from 30 minutes. Empty means no downtime at all.

targets.expr: sort_desc(topk(10, ((1 - max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_uptime_ratio{organization=~"$organization|",window="30d"})) * 2592000) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"} > 0))

defaults.noValue: No downtime in the last 30 days

panels.title: Performance
panels.description: Check durations, failures and freshness. Filtered by Type, Tag and Monitor.

panels.title: Check duration
panels.description: Check duration per monitor as a 15-minute moving average of the latest-check duration (logarithmic axis, so 30 ms DNS lookups and 10 s browser checks fit on one chart). Legend: mean, max and last over the range — click a name to isolate it, Ctrl/Cmd-click to add more. Heartbeat monitors have no duration.

panels.title: Check performance · 24 hours
panels.description: Per monitor: duration of the latest check, mean duration over 24 hours, checks run and failed in 24 hours (all locations), success rate, and how long ago the latest check ran. Freshness compares that age with the configured interval plus 2 minutes of cache and scrape lag: Late after 1.5×, Stale after 3× (heartbeats are evaluated every minute). Failed = failed checks in 24 hours as a bar scaled to the worst monitor, amber from 1, red from 50. Individual failures are normal noise (alerting uses confirmed incidents) — use this to spot flaky targets.

targets.expr: (max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_last_check_duration_seconds{organization=~"$organization|"})) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

(max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_avg_duration_24h_seconds{organization=~"$organization|"})) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

(sum by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_checks_24h{organization=~"$organization|"})) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

(sum by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_checks_24h{organization=~"$organization|",result="failure"})) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

(sum by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_checks_24h{organization=~"$organization|",result="success"}) / sum by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_checks_24h{organization=~"$organization|"} > 0)) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

(time() - max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_last_check_timestamp_seconds{organization=~"$organization|"})) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

((time() - max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_last_check_timestamp_seconds{organization=~"$organization|"})) / (max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_check_interval_seconds{organization=~"$organization|"}) + 120)) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name, type) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

panels.title: Certificates, domains & heartbeats
panels.description: Expiry countdowns and cron check-ins. Filtered by Type, Tag and Monitor.

panels.title: TLS certificates
panels.description: Certificate notAfter for every SSL monitor, soonest first. Days left = (expiry − now) / 86 400. Red under 7 days, amber under 30. Click a name to open the monitor.

targets.expr: ((max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_ssl_certificate_expiry_timestamp_seconds{organization=~"$organization|"}) - time()) / 86400) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

defaults.noValue: No SSL monitors in this selection

panels.title: Domain registrations
panels.description: Registration expiry from RDAP for every domain monitor, soonest first. Days left = (expiry − now) / 86 400. Red under 7 days, amber under 30. Click a name to open the monitor.

targets.expr: ((max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_domain_expiry_timestamp_seconds{organization=~"$organization|"}) - time()) / 86400) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

defaults.noValue: No domain monitors in this selection

panels.title: Heartbeats
panels.description: Cron jobs and workers that ping WatchFor. Last ping = time since the last real check-in; Expected = the configured period. Status turns red once the grace period has passed without a ping (confirmed missed run).

targets.expr: (time() - max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_heartbeat_last_ping_timestamp_seconds{organization=~"$organization|"})) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

(max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_check_interval_seconds{organization=~"$organization|"}) and on (organization, monitor_id) max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_heartbeat_last_ping_timestamp_seconds{organization=~"$organization|"})) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

(max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_monitor_state{organization=~"$organization|"}) and on (organization, monitor_id) max by (organization, monitor_id) (watchfor_heartbeat_last_ping_timestamp_seconds{organization=~"$organization|"})) * on (organization, monitor_id) group_left (name) watchfor_monitor_info{organization=~"$organization|",type=~"$type",tags=~"(.*,)?($tag)(,.*)?",name=~"$monitor"}

defaults.noValue: No heartbeat monitors in this selection

panels.title: Hosts
panels.description: Servers running the WatchFor host agent. Not affected by Type, Tag or Monitor.

panels.title: Hosts by state
panels.description: Share of hosts per agent liveness state: Online, Stale (missed a few pushes), Offline (host incident opened), Never seen (agent installed but never connected).

panels.title: Host inventory
panels.description: Every host with its OS, CPU architecture and agent version. Status: Online when the agent pushed recently, otherwise Not reporting. Last seen = time since the last agent push (Never = the agent has not connected yet). Click a host to open it in WatchFor.

targets.expr: (max by (organization, host_id) (watchfor_host_up{organization=~"$organization|"})) * on (organization, host_id) group_left (name, os, arch, agent_version) watchfor_host_info{organization=~"$organization|"}

(time() - max by (organization, host_id) (watchfor_host_last_seen_timestamp_seconds{organization=~"$organization|"})) * on (organization, host_id) group_left (name, os, arch, agent_version) watchfor_host_info{organization=~"$organization|"}

panels.title: Host availability
panels.description: Agent liveness per host over the selected range: green online, red not reporting (stale, offline or never connected).

panels.title: About this dashboard
panels.description: How the data gets here and how to read it.

options.content:
### WatchFor · Prometheus overview

Fleet health, monitor status, incident-based uptime against an SLO, check performance, certificate / domain expiry,
heartbeats and host agents — from the WatchFor Prometheus endpoint. Every panel has an **ⓘ** with what it shows.

**Two ways to scrape (both work with this dashboard)**

| | Native endpoint | Open-source exporter |
|---|---|---|
| Target | `https://watchfor.io/api/v1/metrics` | `watchfor-io/prometheus-exporter` in your cluster |
| Auth | `Authorization: Bearer wf_live_…` (API key, `read` scope) | the exporter holds the key(s), Prometheus needs none |
| Labels | no `organization` label (one org per key) | adds `organization="<slug>"` to every series, many orgs per exporter |

```yaml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: watchfor
    scheme: https
    metrics_path: /api/v1/metrics
    scrape_interval: 60s          # the body is cached for 60 s; faster scrapes get the same data
    authorization:
      credentials: wf_live_xxxxxxxxxxxx
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["watchfor.io"]
```

Optional query parameters: `tag`, `type`, `monitor_id` (narrow the per-monitor series) and `include_hosts=false`.
Requires the Pro plan or higher; the metrics bucket is 30 requests / minute per organization.

**Reading it**

* *Up / Down* follows confirmed incidents, exactly like the WatchFor dashboard — a single failed check never marks a monitor down.
* *Uptime* is incident-based (confirmed critical downtime, maintenance excluded), the same number as SLA reports.
* The **SLO target** variable recolours the uptime cells and recomputes the error budget.
* Per-object series carry only `monitor_id` / `host_id`; names, types, targets and tags come from the `*_info` series via
  `* on(monitor_id) group_left(name, type) watchfor_monitor_info`.
* *Data age* is the age of the cached body plus your scrape interval; above a few minutes, check the scrape job.
